sanskrit: daṇḍapāṇir acintyātmā sarvabhūtavināśakṛt vaivasvato dharmarājo vimānenāvabhāsayan
english: Staff in hand, of inscrutable nature, the destroyer of all beings — Yama, the son of Vivasvat and king of righteousness, came illuminating the sky with his celestial chariot.

sanskrit: trīṃl lokān guhyakāṃś caiva gandharvāṃś ca sapannagān dvitīya iva mārtaṇḍo yugānte samupasthite
english: Lighting up the three worlds along with the Guhyakas, the Gandharvas, and the serpents, he appeared like a second sun risen at the end of an age.

sanskrit: bhānumanti vicitrāṇi śikharāṇi mahāgireḥ samāsthāyārjunaṃ tatra dadṛśus tapasānvitam
english: Occupying the radiant and many-hued peaks of that great mountain, they beheld Arjuna there, absorbed in his austerities.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād bhagavān airāvataśirogataḥ ājagāma sahendrāṇyā śakraḥ suragaṇair vṛtaḥ
english: Then in a moment the blessed Śakra, mounted on Airāvata's head and accompanied by Indrāṇī, came surrounded by the hosts of gods.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani śuśubhe tārakārājaḥ sitam abhram ivāsthitaḥ
english: With a white parasol held above his head, the lord of stars shone like a white cloud risen in the sky.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamāno gandharvair ṛṣibhiś ca tapodhanaiḥ śṛṅgaṃ gireḥ samāsādya tasthau sūrya ivoditaḥ
english: Praised by the Gandharvas and the sages rich in austerity, he alighted on the peak of the mountain and stood there like the risen sun.

sanskrit: atha meghasvano dhīmān vyājahāra śubhāṃ giram yamaḥ paramadharmajño dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āsthitaḥ
english: Then wise Yama, whose voice was like a thunder-cloud, the supreme knower of righteousness, stationed in the southern quarter, spoke an auspicious word.

sanskrit: arjunārjuna paśyāsmāṃl lokapālān samāgatān dṛṣṭiṃ te vitarāmo 'dya bhavān arho hi darśanam
english: "O Arjuna, Arjuna — behold us, the Guardians of the Worlds, assembled here! We grant you our sight today; you are indeed worthy of beholding us."

sanskrit: pūrvarṣir amitātmā tvaṃ naro nāma mahābalaḥ niyogād brahmaṇas tāta martyatāṃ samupāgataḥ tvaṃ vāsavasamudbhūto mahāvīryaparākramaḥ
english: "You are the ancient seer Nara of boundless soul and great strength, O dear one, who by Brahmā's decree has taken on mortal form. You are born of Vāsava and endowed with immeasurable valour and prowess."

sanskrit: kṣatraṃ cāgnisamasparśaṃ bhāradvājena rakṣitam dānavāś ca mahāvīryā ye manuṣyatvam āgatāḥ nivātakavacāś caiva saṃsādhyāḥ kurunandana
english: "The warrior order, fierce as fire and protected by the son of Bhāradvāja, and the mighty Dānavas who have taken human birth, and the Nivāta-Kavachas too — all must be vanquished by you, O joy of the Kurus."

sanskrit: pitur mamāṃśo devasya sarvalokapratāpinaḥ karṇaḥ sa sumahāvīryas tvayā vadhyo dhanaṃjaya
english: "Karṇa, who is a portion of my father the god who scorches all the worlds, that mighty hero — he must be slain by you, O Dhanañjaya."

sanskrit: aṃśāś ca kṣitisaṃprāptā devagandharvarakṣasām tayā nipātitā yuddhe svakarmaphalanirjitām gatiṃ prāpsyanti kaunteya yathāsvam arikarśana
english: "And the partial incarnations of gods, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas who have descended to earth — those slain by you in battle will each attain the fate earned by their own deeds, O scorcher of foes, O son of Kuntī."

sanskrit: akṣayā tava kīrtiś ca loke sthāsyati phalguna tvayā sākṣān mahādevas toṣito hi mahāmṛdhe laghvī vasumatī cāpi kartavyā viṣṇunā saha
english: "Your fame shall abide imperishable in the world, O Phalguna. Mahādeva himself has been satisfied by you in great battle, and the earth too shall be made light together with Viṣṇu."

sanskrit: gṛhāṇāstraṃ mahābāho daṇḍam aprativāraṇam anenāstreṇa sumahat tvaṃ hi karma kariṣyasi
english: "Receive this weapon, O mighty-armed one — the staff that none can resist. With this weapon you shall accomplish a very great deed."

sanskrit: pratijagrāha tat pārtho vidhivat kurunandanaḥ samantraṃ sopacāraṃ ca samokṣaṃ sanivartanam
english: Pārtha, that joy of the Kurus, received it with full ritual — along with its mantras, its mode of worship, the method of release, and the method of recall.

sanskrit: tato jaladharaśyāmo varuṇo yādasāṃ patiḥ paścimāṃ diśam āsthāya giram uccārayan prabhuḥ
english: Then Varuṇa, dark as a rain-cloud, lord of the aquatic creatures, stationed in the western quarter, raised his voice and spoke, the mighty one.

sanskrit: pārtha kṣatriyamukhyas tvaṃ kṣatradharme vyavasthitaḥ paśya māṃ pṛthutāmrākṣa varuṇo 'smi jaleśvaraḥ
english: "O Pārtha, foremost of warriors, firmly established in the warrior's duty — behold me, O broad-eyed one with coppery gaze. I am Varuṇa, lord of waters."

sanskrit: mayā samudyatān pāśān vāruṇān anivāraṇān pratigṛhṇīṣva kaunteya sarahasyanivartanān
english: "Receive from me these Varuṇa nooses I have raised, which none can resist, O son of Kuntī — along with the secret of their recall."

sanskrit: ebhis tadā mayā vīra saṃgrāme tārakāmaye daiteyānāṃ sahasrāṇi saṃyatāni mahātmanām
english: "With these, O hero, in the battle of the stars against the demons, I had bound thousands of the great-souled Daityas."

sanskrit: tasmād imān mahāsattva matprasādāt samutthitān gṛhāṇa na hi te mucyed antako 'py ātatāyinaḥ
english: "Therefore take these, O great being, arisen through my grace. Not even Death himself could escape them if he were a violent aggressor."

sanskrit: anena tvaṃ yadāstreṇa saṃgrāme vicariṣyasi tadā niḥkṣatriyā bhūmir bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "When you move through battle with this weapon, the earth shall be stripped of its warrior class — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tataḥ kailāsanilayo dhanādhyakṣo 'bhyabhāṣata datteṣv astreṣu divyeṣu varuṇena yamena ca
english: Then Kubera, whose abode is Kailāsa, the lord of wealth, spoke out, after Varuṇa and Yama had each bestowed their divine weapons.

sanskrit: savyasācin mahābāho pūrvadeva sanātana sahāsmābhir bhavāñ śrāntaḥ purākalpeṣu nityaśaḥ
english: "O Savyasācin, mighty-armed one, O ancient primeval god, you have always toiled alongside us in the ages of old."

sanskrit: matto 'pi tvaṃ gṛhāṇāstram antardhānaṃ priyaṃ mama ojastejodyutiharaṃ prasvāpanam arātihan
english: "From me too receive this weapon — the dear Antardhana, my favourite: it robs the enemy of vitality, brilliance, and radiance, and casts foes into a deep sleep, O slayer of enemies."

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahābāhur vidhivat kurunandanaḥ kauberam api jagrāha divyam astraṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Then mighty Arjuna, that great-armed joy of the Kurus, received with full ceremony the divine Kubera weapon as well.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd devarājaḥ pārtham akliṣṭakāriṇam sāntvayañ ślakṣṇayā vācā meghadundubhinisvanaḥ
english: Then the king of the gods, whose voice rang like a cloud-drum, addressed Pārtha the effortless doer, consoling him with gentle words.

sanskrit: kuntīmātar mahābāho tvam īśānaḥ purātanaḥ parāṃ siddhim anuprāptaḥ sākṣād devagatiṃ gataḥ
english: "O son of Kuntī, O mighty-armed one, you are the ancient lord Īśāna himself. You have attained the highest perfection and have in truth reached the state of the gods."

sanskrit: devakāryaṃ hi sumahat tvayā kāryam ariṃdama āroḍhavyas tvayā svargaḥ sajjībhava mahādyute
english: "A very great divine task must be performed by you, O subduer of foes. You must ascend to heaven — make yourself ready, O greatly radiant one."

sanskrit: ratho mātalisaṃyukta āgantā tvatkṛte mahīm tatra te 'haṃ pradāsyāmi divyāny astrāṇi kaurava
english: "A chariot yoked by Mātali will come to earth for your sake. There I shall bestow upon you the divine weapons, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā lokapālāṃs tu sametān girimūrdhani jagāma vismayaṃ dhīmān kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Beholding those Guardians of the Worlds assembled on the mountain's summit, wise Dhanañjaya, the son of Kuntī, was overcome with wonder.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mahātejā lokapālān samāgatān pūjayām āsa vidhivad vāgbhir adbhiḥ phalair api
english: Then the greatly radiant Arjuna honoured those assembled Guardians of the Worlds with due ceremony — with words, with water, and with fruits.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratiyayur devāḥ pratipūjya dhanaṃjayam yathāgatena vibudhāḥ sarve kāmamanojavāḥ
english: Then the gods honoured Dhanañjaya in return and departed, all those wise ones swift as wish and thought, each by the way he had come.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno mudaṃ lebhe labdhāstraḥ puruṣarṣabhaḥ kṛtārtham iva cātmānaṃ sa mene pūrṇamānasaḥ
english: Then Arjuna, that bull among men, having received the weapons, felt great joy. With a full heart he deemed himself as one whose purpose had been fulfilled.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca gateṣu lokapāleṣu pārthaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ cintayām āsa rājendra devarājarathāgamam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the Guardians of the Worlds had departed, Pārtha the destroyer of enemies, O king of kings, began to contemplate the coming of the king of gods' chariot.

sanskrit: tataś cintayamānasya guḍākeśasya dhīmataḥ ratho mātalisaṃyukta ājagāma mahāprabhaḥ
english: And even as the wise Guḍākeśa was pondering this, there came the greatly resplendent chariot yoked by Mātali.

sanskrit: nabho vitimiraṃ kurvañ jaladān pāṭayann iva diśaḥ saṃpūrayan nādair mahāmegharavopamaiḥ
english: Clearing the sky of darkness, as if splitting the rain-clouds asunder, filling the quarters with sounds like the roar of great storm-clouds.

sanskrit: asayaḥ śaktayo bhīmā gadāś cograpradarśanāḥ divyaprabhāvāḥ prāsāś ca vidyutaś ca mahāprabhāḥ
english: Swords, terrible lances, maces of fearsome aspect, divine-powered javelins, and great blazing lightnings adorned it.

sanskrit: tathaivāśanayas tatra cakrayuktā huḍāguḍāḥ vāyusphoṭāḥ sanirghātā barhimeghanibhasvanāḥ
english: And likewise thunderbolts fitted with wheels, rumbling war-engines, wind-blasts with the crash of thunder, sounding like fire-bearing clouds.

sanskrit: tatra nāgā mahākāyā jvalitāsyāḥ sudāruṇāḥ sitābhrakūṭapratimāḥ saṃhatāś ca yathopalāḥ
english: There too were serpents of enormous body with blazing mouths, most terrible, resembling peaks of white cloud, clustered together like boulders.

sanskrit: daśa vājisahasrāṇi harīṇāṃ vātaraṃhasām vahanti yaṃ netramuṣaṃ divyaṃ māyāmayaṃ ratham
english: Ten thousand tawny steeds swift as the wind drew that divine, illusion-wrought chariot that robbed the eye of clear sight.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan mahānīlaṃ vaijayantaṃ mahāprabham dhvajam indīvaraśyāmaṃ vaṃśaṃ kanakabhūṣaṃ
english: There he saw the great dark-blue Vaijayanta banner of immense splendour, dark as a blue lotus, its staff adorned with gold.

sanskrit: tasmin rathe sthitaṃ sūtaṃ taptahemavibhūṣitam dṛṣṭvā pārtho mahābāhur devam evānvatarkayat
english: Seeing the charioteer standing in that chariot, adorned with refined gold, mighty-armed Pārtha surmised at once that it must be a god.

sanskrit: tathā tarkayatas tasya phalgunasyātha mātaliḥ saṃnataḥ praśrito bhūtvā vākyam arjunam abravīt
english: And as Phalguna was reasoning thus, Mātali bowed low with humility and spoke these words to Arjuna.

sanskrit: bho bho śakrātmaja śrīmāñ śakras tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati ārohatu bhavāñ śīghraṃ ratham indrasya saṃmatam
english: "Ho, O glorious son of Śakra! Śakra desires to see you. May your honour quickly ascend the chariot of Indra with my blessing."

sanskrit: āha mām amaraśreṣṭhaḥ pitā tava śatakratuḥ kuntīsutam iha prāptaṃ paśyantu tridaśālayāḥ
english: "The foremost of the immortals, your father of a hundred sacrifices, bade me: 'Let the dwellers of heaven behold the son of Kuntī arrived here.'"

sanskrit: eṣa śakraḥ parivṛto devair ṛṣigaṇais tathā gandharvair apsarobhiś ca tvāṃ didṛkṣuḥ pratīkṣate
english: "Śakra, surrounded by gods and hosts of sages, and also by Gandharvas and Apsaras, eagerly awaits and expects you, longing to behold you."

sanskrit: asmāl lokād devalokaṃ pākaśāsanaśāsanāt āroha tvaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ labdhāstraḥ punar eṣyasi
english: "By the command of Pāka-shasana ascend with me from this world to the world of the gods; having obtained the weapons, you will return again."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca mātale gaccha śīghraṃ tvam ārohasva rathottamam rājasūyāśvamedhānāṃ śatair api sudurlabham
english: Arjuna said: O Mātali, go quickly — you first ascend the supreme chariot, which is exceedingly hard to obtain even by hundreds of Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: pārthivaiḥ sumahābhāgair yajvabhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ daivatair vā samāroḍhuṃ dānavair vā rathottamam
english: "This supreme chariot is not to be mounted even by kings of the greatest fortune, by sacrificers of abundant gifts, nor by gods or Dānavas."

sanskrit: nātaptatapasā śakya eṣa divyo mahārathaḥ draṣṭuṃ vāpy atha vā spraṣṭum āroḍhuṃ kuta eva tu
english: "Without having practised fierce austerities, this divine great chariot cannot even be seen, let alone touched — much less mounted."

sanskrit: tvayi pratiṣṭhite sādho rathasthe sthiravājini paścād aham athārokṣye sukṛtī satpathaṃ yathā
english: "When you, O good one, are established on the chariot with the horses steady, then I shall mount afterwards, like a man of good deeds following the righteous path."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā mātaliḥ śakrasārathiḥ āruroha rathaṃ śīghraṃ hayān yeme ca raśmibhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing those words of Arjuna, Mātali the charioteer of Śakra quickly ascended the chariot and controlled the horses with the reins.

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno hṛṣṭamanā gaṅgāyām āplutaḥ śuciḥ jajāpa japyaṃ kaunteyo vidhivat kurunandanaḥ
english: Then Arjuna, joyful in heart, bathed in the Gaṅgā, purified himself, and the son of Kuntī, that joy of the Kurus, performed his prescribed recitations with due ceremony.

sanskrit: tataḥ pitṝn yathānyāyaṃ tarpayitvā yathāvidhi mandaraṃ śailarājaṃ tam āpraṣṭum upacakrame
english: Then, having duly satisfied the ancestral spirits with water according to rule, he approached that king of mountains, Mandara, to take his leave.

sanskrit: sādhūnāṃ dharmaśīlānāṃ munīnāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām tvaṃ sadā saṃśrayaḥ śaila svargamārgābhikāṅkṣiṇām
english: "You are ever the refuge, O mountain, of the virtuous and righteous, of sages of holy deeds, of those who aspire to the path of heaven."

sanskrit: tvatprasādāt sadā śaila brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā viśaḥ svargaṃ prāptāś caranti sma devaiḥ saha gatavyathāḥ
english: "By your grace, O mountain, Brāhmaṇas, warriors, and merchants have ever gained heaven and move there free of sorrow together with the gods."

sanskrit: adrirāja mahāśaila munisaṃśraya tīrthavan gacchāmy āmantrayāmi tvāṃ sukham asmy uṣitas tvayi
english: "O king of mountains, great peak, refuge of sages, rich in holy fords — I take my leave of you as I depart. I have dwelt happily in you."

sanskrit: tava sānūni kuñjāś ca nadyaḥ prasravaṇāni ca tīrthāni ca supuṇyāni mayā dṛṣṭāny anekaśaḥ
english: "Your ridges, your groves, your rivers and springs, your greatly sacred fords — all these have I seen again and again."

sanskrit: evam uktvārjunaḥ śailam āmantrya paravīrahā āruroha rathaṃ divyaṃ dyotayann iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Having spoken thus and taken leave of the mountain, Arjuna the destroyer of enemy heroes mounted the divine chariot, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: sa tenādityarūpeṇa divyenādbhutakarmaṇā ūrdhvam ācakrame dhīmān prahṛṣṭaḥ kurunandanaḥ
english: On that solar-formed, divine chariot of marvellous workmanship, wise Arjuna, the joy of the Kurus, ascended upward in great delight.

sanskrit: so 'darśanapathaṃ yātvā martyānāṃ bhūmicāriṇām dadarśādbhutarūpāṇi vimānāni sahasraśaḥ
english: Having travelled beyond the path of sight of mortals who walk on earth, he beheld thousands upon thousands of celestial cars of wondrous form.

sanskrit: na tatra sūryaḥ somo vā dyotate na ca pāvakaḥ svayaiva prabhayā tatra dyotante puṇyalabdhayā
english: There neither sun nor moon gives light, nor does fire — those there shine by their own radiance, won by their merits.

sanskrit: tārārūpāṇi yānīha dṛśyante dyutimanti vai dīpavad viprakṛṣṭatvād aṇūni sumahānty api
english: Those which appear here below in the forms of stars, brilliant though they be, appear tiny like lamps because of their great distance — though they are vast in truth.

sanskrit: tāni tatra prabhāsvanti rūpavanti ca pāṇḍavaḥ dadarśa sveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣu dīptimanti svayārciṣā
english: The son of Pāṇḍu beheld those very same — luminous, beautiful, blazing with their own flames in their own dwelling-places.

sanskrit: tatra rājarṣayaḥ siddhā vīrāś ca nihatā yudhi tapasā ca jitasvargāḥ saṃpetuḥ śatasaṃghaśaḥ
english: There royal sages and siddhas, and heroes slain in battle, and those who had conquered heaven by austerity, came streaming together in hundreds of companies.

sanskrit: gandharvāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi sūryajvalanatejasām guhyakānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ
english: Thousands of Gandharvas blazing with the energy of the sun, Guhyakas, sages, and likewise hosts of Apsaras were there.

sanskrit: lokān ātmaprabhān paśyan phalguno vismayānvitaḥ papraccha mātaliṃ prītyā sa cāpy enam uvāca ha
english: Beholding those self-luminous worlds, Phalguna was filled with wonder and questioned Mātali out of curiosity; and Mātali indeed answered him.

sanskrit: ete sukṛtinaḥ pārtha sveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣv avasthitāḥ yān dṛṣṭavān asi vibho tārārūpāṇi bhūtale
english: "These, O Pārtha, are the meritorious ones established in their own abodes — those which you saw, O mighty lord, appearing in the form of stars on the earth below."

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat sthitaṃ dvāri sitaṃ vaijayinaṃ gajam airāvataṃ caturdantaṃ kailāsam iva śṛṅgiṇam
english: Then he saw standing at the gate the white victorious elephant Airāvata, four-tusked, like a peaked mountain of Kailāsa.

sanskrit: sa siddhamārgam ākramya kurupāṇḍavasattamaḥ vyarocata yathā pūrvaṃ māndhātā pārthivottamaḥ
english: Traversing the path of the perfected ones, that greatest of the Kuru-Pāṇḍava lineage shone like Māndhātā of old, the foremost of kings.

sanskrit: aticakrāma lokān sa rājñāṃ rājīvalocanaḥ tato dadarśa śakrasya purīṃ tām amarāvatīm
english: The lotus-eyed hero passed beyond the worlds of kings and then beheld that city of Śakra, Amarāvatī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa dadarśa purīṃ ramyāṃ siddhacāraṇasevitām sarvartukusumaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pādapair upaśobhitām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He beheld that delightful city, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, adorned with sacred trees bearing the blossoms of every season.

sanskrit: tatra saugandhikānāṃ sa drumāṇāṃ puṇyagandhinām upavījyamāno miśreṇa vāyunā puṇyagandhinā
english: There, fanned by the blended breeze that carries the holy fragrance of the saugandhika trees with their sacred perfume,

sanskrit: nandanaṃ ca vanaṃ divyam apsarogaṇasevitam dadarśa divyakusumair āhvayadbhir iva drumaiḥ
english: he also beheld the divine grove of Nandana, frequented by troops of Apsaras, its trees seeming to beckon with their divine blossoms.

sanskrit: nātaptatapasā śakyo draṣṭuṃ nānāhitāgninā sa lokaḥ puṇyakartṝṇāṃ nāpi yuddhaparāṅmukhaiḥ
english: That world of the doers of merit cannot be seen by one who has not practised fierce austerities, nor by one who has not kindled the sacred fires, nor by those who turn their backs in battle.

sanskrit: nāyajvabhir nānṛtakair na vedaśrutivarjitaiḥ nānāplutāṅgais tīrtheṣu yajñadānabahiṣkṛtaiḥ
english: Not by those who have not performed sacrifices, not by liars, not by those ignorant of Vedic learning, not by those who have not bathed in sacred fords, not by those excluded from sacrifice and charity.

sanskrit: nāpi yajñahanaiḥ kṣudrair draṣṭuṃ śakyaḥ kathaṃ cana pānapair gurutalpaiś ca māṃsādair vā durātmabhiḥ
english: Nor can it in any way be seen by the petty destroyers of sacrifices, by drunkards, by violators of a guru's bed, by flesh-eaters, or by evil-souled persons.

sanskrit: sa tad divyaṃ vanaṃ paśyan divyagītanināditam praviveśa mahābāhuḥ śakrasya dayitāṃ purīm
english: Beholding that divine grove resonant with divine song, the mighty-armed one entered the beloved city of Śakra.

sanskrit: tatra devavimānāni kāmagāni sahasraśaḥ saṃsthitāny abhiyātāni dadarśāyutaśas tadā
english: There he then beheld thousands upon tens of thousands of divine celestial cars at rest and in motion, moving at will.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamāno gandharvair apsarobhiś ca pāṇḍavaḥ puṣpagandhavahaiḥ puṇyair vāyubhiś cānuvījitaḥ
english: The son of Pāṇḍu, praised by Gandharvas and Apsaras, fanned by holy breezes bearing the fragrance of flowers, entered the city.
